bull.b: The agreement creates a defined pathway to commercialize Loop’s technology in India and other territories. Royalty-linked economics could provide recurring revenue if ELITe successfully builds facilities and scales recycled polymer production.

Exclusive marketing rights give Loop influence over customer contracts, pricing and volumes while adding sales-linked fee potential. This aligns Loop with product adoption and may broaden commercialization without requiring it to fund every operating activity directly.

Adding an experienced independent director strengthens oversight and capital-markets expertise during a financially constrained commercialization phase. Independent governance can improve strategic discipline, stakeholder confidence and evaluation of future funding or partnerships.

bear.b: Extremely negative margins and a shrinking revenue base indicate that the business has not yet achieved commercial scale or operating leverage. Sustained losses could limit investment capacity and increase dependence on external funding while projects mature.

Ongoing cash consumption reduces flexibility to fund technology development, commercialization and project obligations. Unless licensing or operating receipts scale materially, repeated financing needs could dilute shareholders or constrain execution of the company’s strategy.

Dual listing deficiencies create a meaningful governance and financing risk over the next several months. Potential loss of the current Nasdaq listing could reduce market access, limit investor participation and complicate efforts to raise capital for commercialization.
